set.q: Identify all of the following 3 structures that are membrane bound: 1) Lysosome; 2) Cell Wall; 3) Ribosome.
Identify all of the following three compounds that are soluble in water at room temperature: 1) AgCl; 2) NH_4Cl; 3) KCl.
Simplify the fraction with numerator 25 and denominator 1/2 + 1/3.
Identify all of the following three particles that experience the strong force: 1) Proton; 2) Electron; 3) Pion.
Order the following three marine provinces by increasing average slope 1) Abyssal plain; 2) Oceanic trench; 3) Continental rise.
Select all of the following three types of hepatitis that are caused by positive sense RNA viruses. 1) Hepatitis A; 2) Hepatitis B; 3) Hepatitis C.

Travis is looking into the logistics behind fossil fuel energy generation. Rank the following three forms of fossil fuel energy by increasing average energy density by mass: 1) Coal; 2) Petroleum; 3) Natural gas.
Order the following three metamorphic rocks by increasing metamorphic grade: 1) Schist; 2) Slate; 3) Gneiss.
Rank the following three compounds in order of increasing lattice energy: 1) Sodium chloride; 2) Potassium chloride; 3) Magnesium chloride.
Which of the following four objects can produce a real image? 1) Convex lens; 2) Concave lens; 3) Convex mirror; 4) Concave mirror.

In an effort to comply with state energy laws, Hawaii closed its last coal-fired power plant in 2022. While this plant was in operation, it primarily utilized sub-bituminous coal for power generation. Identify all of the following three varieties of coal that have a higher rank than sub-bituminous coal: 1) Bituminous coal; 2) Lignite; 3) Anthracite.

In order to meet the baseload energy demand of consumers, power grids must incorporate "firm" power sources that ensure grid stability. Identify all of the following four renewable energy sources that could be considered "firm": 1) Solar; 2) Wind; 3) Geothermal; 4) Biomass.
Identify all of the following three hydrocarbons that would be considered saturated: 1) Propane; 2) Propene; 3) Propyne.
Rank the following three hydrologic reservoirs in increasing share of the Earth's total freshwater budget: 1) Atmosphere; 2) Glaciers and ice sheets; 3) Groundwater.
Order the following three silicate minerals by increasing resistance to weathering: 1) Olivine; 2) Amphibole; 3) Orthoclase.
Select all of the following blood types that are possible between a AB+ father and a B- mother: 1) A-; 2) AB+; 3) O+; 4) B-.
Identify all of the following 3 barriers that are considered to be prezygotic. 1) Gametic isolation; 2) Temporal isolation; 3) Hybrid breakdown.
Identify all of the four fundamental forces that have infinite range. 1) Strong nuclear; 2) Weak nuclear; 3) Gravitational; 4) Electromagnetic.
Order the following three types of galaxies by increasing median age of their stars: 1) Elliptical; 2) Spiral; 3) Lenticular.
Select all of the following 3 that play a role in the cell mediated immune response: 1) Antigen presenting cells; 2) Cytotoxic T cells; 3) NK cells.

Sam is studying the relative strength of attractive and repulsive forces between molecules. Rank the following three intermolecular forces in order of increasing strength: 1) London Dispersion Forces; 2) Dipole-dipole forces; 3) Ion-dipole forces.
Order the following 3 elements in terms of increasing third ionization energy: 1) Aluminum; 2) Magnesium; 3) Barium.

If Sola ran the first two miles of a race at 30 miles per hour, and ran the next two miles of a race at 10 miles per hour, which of the following is equal to his average speed across the entire race, in miles per hour?
A particle has velocity exactly equal to the escape velocity of the Earth. What shape is the trajectory of this particle?
Order the following three glacial formations by increasing distance from the peak of a mountain: 1) Terminal moraine; 2) Medial moraine; 3) Cirque.
Rank the following 4 acids in terms of increasing acidity: 1) HCl; 2) HBr; 3) HBrO; 4) HBrO2.
Identify all of the following three intrusive igneous features that would be considered concordant: 1) Dike; 2) Sill; 3) Laccolith.
Order the following 3 steps in corresponding order of the central dogma: 1) DNA Replication; 2) Transcription; 3) Translation.
If you have an AB- father and a B+ mother, what is the probability that hemolytic disease of the newborn occurs?

A zeroth-order reaction starts with an initial reactant concentration of 0.2 M. Given that the rate constant of this reaction is 3.0 × 10^-3 M s^-1, calculate the initial half-life of the reaction to two significant figures.
Rank the following three stages in the movement of electricity through the grid system by increasing average voltage: 1) Transmission lines; 2) Distribution lines; 3) Generation facilities.
Rank the following three water masses by increasing average density: 1) North Atlantic Deep Water; 2) Mediterranean Intermediate Water; 3) Antarctic Bottom Water.
Order the following 3 steps of PCR in decreasing temperature: 1) Denaturation; 2) Annealing; 3) Extension.
Order the following three nonmetals in order of increasing magnitude of electron affinity in their ground state: 1) Oxygen; 2) Sulfur; 3) Phosphorus.
Peter is trapped inside a comet! Order the following layers of a comet from innermost to outermost: 1) Halo; 2) Coma; 3) Nucleus.
By name or number, select all of the following species for which Chargaff's Rule does not apply: 1) HIV; 2) Hepatitis B; 3) Streptococcus pyogenes.
Order the following three layers of the ocean by increasing depth: 1) Epipelagic; 2) Mesopelagic; 3) Abyssopelagic.
Which of the following best describes the change in seismic body wave velocity going from the lower mantle to the outer core, and the outer core to the inner core, respectively?
Order the following three types of unit cells in order of increasing packing efficiency: 1) Simple cubic; 2) Face-centered cubic; 3) Body-centered cubic.
Order the following three stages in the evolution of a solar-mass star from first to last to occur: 1) Red giant; 2) White dwarf; 3) Main-sequence.
Order the following three numbers from least to greatest: 1) e^π; 2) π^e; 3) 3^3.

In contrast with primary batteries, which are not rechargeable, secondary batteries can be discharged and recharged multiple times. Identify all of the following three types of batteries that would be considered secondary: 1) Alkaline; 2) Lead-acid; 3) Lithium-ion.

Fissile materials break apart easily when bombarded by neutrons, and are used to sustain chain reactions in nuclear power plants. Identify all of the following three isotopes of Uranium that are considered fissile: 1) Uranium-233; 2) Uranium-235; 3) Uranium-238.
By name or number, order the following three phases of prophase I from earliest to latest in the cell cycle: 1) Zygotene; 2) Diplodene; 3) Leptotene.
Identify all of the following three aqueous species that would be classified as Lewis acids: 1) AlCl3; 2) BF3; 3) NH3.

The Hawaii State Government is currently considering liquified natural gas, LNG, as a potential “bridge fuel” in its transition to clean energy generation. Order the following four steps in the production of LNG from first to last: 1) Liquefaction; 2) Purification; 3) Shipping; 4) Regasification.
Rank the following three solids by increasing melting point: 1) Iron oxide; 2) Sodium fluoride; 3) Boron nitride.
What is the smallest positive angle x, in radians, that satisfies the equation sin(2x) * sec(x) = 1?

Nuclear reactors use heat transfer fluids, also known as coolants, to pull thermal energy from the reactor core and turn it into usable power. Order the following three types of nuclear reactors by increasing specific heat capacity of their respective coolant: 1) Heavy water reactors; 2) Liquid metal fast reactors; 3) Molten salt reactors.

Order the following steps of DNA replication initiation in bacteria chronologically. 1) The hydrogen bonds of the DNA unwinding element are broken due to DnaA-ATP complexes; 2) The OriC is recognized by DnaA proteins; 3) Single-stranded binding proteins bind to each of the single stranded DNA and DnaB is recruited.
Order the following three oxide compounds by increasing pH in a 0.1 M aqueous solution: 1) Potassium oxide; 2) Aluminum oxide; 3) Nitrogen dioxide.

A student gets a score of 85 on a math test, while the class mean is 75. Given that the standard deviation for the class is 10 points, which of the following is closest to the percentile of the student's score relative to the rest of the class?
Chris is studying the components of the Sun. Order the following three layers of the Sun's atmosphere in increasing distance from the center of the Sun: 1) Photosphere; 2) Corona; 3) Chromosphere.
Which of the following actions/conditions would be most likely to increase a person's heart rate? 1) Addison's disease; 2) Administration of Atropine; 3) Administration of beta-blockers.

set.c.X: The change in blood clotting effectiveness based on the temperature and pH of blood
set.c.Y: The shift in the peak emission wavelength of light returned from an excited fluorophore
set.c.Z: The change in the solubility of CO2 based on oxygenation percentage of blood

set.q: Sola is genuinely about to crash out. If his probability of crashing out today is 1/2, and the probability that he crashes out the next day is 1/4, and so-on, so that the probability of him crashing out on day n is 1/2^n. To one decimal place, which of the following is closest to the probability that Sola never crashes out?

Identify all of the following three sums that converge: 1) The sum of the reciprocal of every prime number; 2) The sum of the reciprocal of every Fibonacci number; 3) The sum of the reciprocal of every perfect power.
For central force fields, which of the following three proportionalities with distance is considered stable? 1) 2; 2) 0; 3) -2.
Rank the following electrical instruments by increasing resistance: 1) Ohmmeter; 2) Ammeter; 3) Voltmeter.
By name or number, order the three ossicles from most medial to most lateral with respect to the human body: 1) Incus; 2) Malleus; 3) Stapes.

By name or number, select all the following 3 comparisons between hemoglobin and myoglobin that are accurate: 1) Hemoglobin has a larger Hill coefficient than myoglobin; 2) Myoglobin has a higher disassociation constant than hemoglobin; 3) Hemoglobin has a sigmoidal saturation curve, while myoglobin has a hyperbolic saturation curve.
Let f(x) = x^2 - 4x - 3. In the closed interval from 1 to 4, what value of c satisfies the equation f'(c) = [f(4) - f(1)]/3?

List the following three reversible thermodynamic processes in chronological order in an ideal Carnot cycle following isothermal expansion: 1) Isothermal compression; 2) Adiabatic compression; 3) Adiabatic expansion.

Travis is working to plant crops beneath the solar panels in an agrivoltaics system, where shade is maximized directly beneath the center of rotation. Order the following crops that you would find in increasing distance from the center of rotation of the solar panels: 1) Carrots; 2) Lettuce; 3) Peppers.
By name or number, order the following 3 entries by increasing biotic potential: 1) House Mouse; 2) African Elephant; 3) Mosquito.

Travis is trying to create an n-type semiconductor as a part of his new LED light so that he can read Klein before going to sleep. Identify all of the following three elements that would likely be used for n-type doping: 1) Phosphorus; 2) Arsenic; 3) Gallium.
Order the following types of stellar families in increasing median age of their stars: 1) Open clusters; 2) Globular clusters; 3) OB associations.

While high-voltage alternating current, or HVAC, is the most prevalent form of bulk electricity transport, high-voltage direct current, HVDC, is another method that is increasingly being used for long-distance transmission. Identify all of the following three statements that are true about HVAC and HVDC: 1) HVDC doesn't suffer from reactive power losses; 2) HVDC requires more conductors than HVAC; 3) HVDC substations require more complex transformer infrastructure than HVAC.

The reaction H_2 (g) + I_2 (g) --> 2HI (g) at 750 kelvin has K_c= 6.3 × 10^1. David heats a vessel with 0.5 atmospheres of hydrogen gas and 0.5 atmospheres of iodine gas to 750 kelvin and examines the resulting mixture's composition. To one significant figure, what is the final partial pressure of hydrogen iodide in the vessel?
Identify all of the following three types of telescopes that suffer from chromatic aberration: 1) Galilean; 2) Keplerian; 3) Newtonian.
Rank the following four compounds in increasing order of boiling point: 1) Isobutane; 2) Iso-butanol; 3) N-butanol; 4) N-butane.
Which of the following 3D vectors is orthogonal to the vector (2, 0, 7)?
Order the following four soil horizons from the lowest concentration of organic matter to the highest in a typical soil profile: 1) A horizon; 2) B horizon; 3) C horizon; 4) O horizon.
Rank the following three group 16 hydrides by increasing average bond angle: 1) H_2O; 2) H_2S; 3) H_2Se.

Wind shear is a key consideration in the placement of wind turbine systems and is highly dependent on surface topography. Rank the following three locations by increasing wind shear exponent in their vertical profiles: 1) Open ocean; 2) Farmland; 3) Dense forests.

In the upper photic zone, marine phytoplankton require various nutrients in order to sustain life. Order the following three elements by increasing abundance in marine phytoplankton: 1) Nitrogen; 2) Phosphorus; 3) Carbon.
Diana loves to drink copper. However, to do this, she needs to find some copper ores! Order the following minerals in increasing copper content. 1) Turquoise; 2) Malachite; 3) Dioptase.

Presume you are cultivating a short day plant with a critical night length of 12 hours. By name or number, select all of the following 3 scenarios in which the plant will flower: 1) 13 hours of straight darkness; 2) 18 hours of darkness with a flash of white light at the 9 hour mark; 3) 18 hours of darkness with a flash of far red light at the 9 hours mark.

Identify all of the following three statements that are true of SN2 reactions: 1) They are favored by polar aprotic solvents; 2) They are favored by tertiary substrates; 3) If substitution occurs at a chiral center, inverse of configuration is likely to occur.
Identify all of the following three metal hydroxide compounds which are insoluble in water but dissolve under strongly basic conditions: 1) Li(OH); 2) Be(OH)2; 3) Al(OH)3.
Identify all of the following three quantities which may be zero in classical electrodynamics: 1) Curl of magnetic field; 2) Curl of electric field; 3) Divergence of magnetic field.

Biogas, a renewable energy fuel, is formed through the biological breakdown of matter via microbial anaerobic digestion. Order the following three steps in the formation of biogas in chronological order: 1) Acidogenesis; 2) Acetogenesis; 3) Hydrolysis.
Order the following three components of the interstellar medium in order of decreasing average density: 1) H I regions; 2) H II regions; 3) Molecular clouds.

Phosphatidylserine also has a function of supporting cognitive function and protecting brain cells from oxidative damage. Which of the following best describes the connection between the endothelial cells of the blood-brain barrier contributing to this function?
Identify all of the following 3 compounds in their lowest energy conformation whose carbon atoms are planar: 1) Cyclopropane; 2) Cyclobutane; 3) Cyclopentane.

Identify all of the following three statements which are true of the nitrosonium ion, which has formula NO^+: 1) It has a bond order of 3; 2) It is paramagnetic; 3) It forms an acidic solution in water.

Hong Jin is observing active galactic nuclei. Identify all of the following three statements are true about Seyfert galaxies: 1) Seyfert 1 galaxies are brighter than Quasars; 2) Seyfert 1 galaxies typically have narrow emission lines; 3) Seyfert 2 galaxies are typically more luminous than Type I Seyfert galaxies.

Meniere’s Disease is a specific type of sensorineural hearing loss that occurs as a result of hydrops accumulation in the cochlea, and results in a distinctive pattern of hearing loss. Which of the following best describes it?
Rank the following three molecules by increasing bond angle: 1) NH3; 2) NF3; 3) NCl3.
A semiconductor is put on forward bias. Answer the following two questions about this system: 1) Is the resistance of the semiconductor high or low?; 2) Is the anode on the P or N junction?.

In the gasification of biomass or municipal solid waste, thermal conversion in an oxygen-starved environment primarily produces syngas. Which of the following two gases constitute the primary combustible components of syngas?

Identify all of the following three statements that are true about Ocean Thermal Energy Conversion, or OTEC: 1) OTEC has a net-zero carbon footprint; 2) OTEC is only feasible for tropical and subtropical regions; 3) OTEC can provide continuous baseload power.

Identify all of the following statements that are true of minimum-boiling azeotropes: 1) They exhibit negative deviations from Raoult’s Law; 2) IMFs are weaker in the solution than in the pure components; 3) Mixing the components is an endothermic process.

Identify all of the following factors that contribute to trimethylborane being a weaker Lewis acid than boron trifluoride: 1) The methyl groups donate electron density toward boron inductively, whereas the fluorines withdraw it; 2) Hyperconjugation from the C–H bonds of the methyl groups donates electron density into boron's empty 2p orbital; 3) The fluorines donate a lone pair into boron's empty 2p orbital, whereas the methyl groups have none to donate.
Identify all of the following three gases that must be removed from the condenser in a dry steam geothermal plant: 1) Carbon dioxide; 2) Hydrogen sulfide; 3) Water vapor.

Local Hawaiian farms are increasingly integrating feedstocks into their crop production, which can replace petroleum in power-generating facilities. Order the following three forms of biofuel feedstocks from first generation to third generation: 1) Sugarcane; 2) Microalgae; 3) Camelina.
Order the following three orbital subshells by increasing energy: 1) 4f; 2) 5d; 3) 6s.

Order the following four C-H bonds by increasing s-character of the carbon orbital involved in the bond: 1) C–H bond in ethane; 2) C-H bond in benzene; 3) C-H bond in hydrogen cyanide; 4) C-H bond in cyclopropane.
Which of the following best describes the first and second derivatives, respectively, of the charge in a capacitor when it is discharged in an RC circuit?
Kian adds water to magma and notices that it melts at a much lower temperature, a phenomenon known as flux melting. Which of the following best describes why this phenomenon occurs?
set.c.W: Water increases the thermal conductivity of the surrounding mantle rocks, allowing more rapid transfer of heat
set.c.X: Water molecules physically depolymerize the silicate framework
set.c.Y: The total entropy of the solid mineral phase increases, increasing favorability at higher temperatures
set.c.Z: Water acts as a lubricant that reduces friction between mineral grains, causing effective pressure to drop
set.a.t: Water molecules physically depolymerize the silicate framework

set.q: Annexin A5, formerly known as annexin V, is an apoptotic signaler that recognizes phosphatidylserine (PS). By name or number, select all of the following three that interact with PS, and are ATP dependent: 1) Flippase; 2) Floppase; 3) Scramblase.

By name or number, select all of the following 4 scenarios which could result in a positive Ames test: 1) Application of UV light; 2) Application of Propylene Glycol; 3) Application of Ethidium Bromide; 4) Application of Benzene.

In organic chemistry, the A-value measures how much a given substituent prefers the equatorial over the axial position in a cyclohexane ring. Order the following three substituent groups by increasing A-value: 1) Hydroxyl; 2) Fluoro; 3) Tert-butyl.
Identify all of the following methods that can be used to separate a racemic mixture into its component enantiomers: 1) Fractional distillation; 2) Crystallization; 3) Column chromatography.

Owen is singing to Chinese songs during an earthquake. Identify all of the following three measurements that are typically used to deduce the moment magnitude for an earthquake: 1) Peak wave amplitude; 2) Average fault slip; 3) Rupture area.
By name or number, order the following 5 layers of the epiphyseal plate from the closest to furthest from the diaphysis: 1) Zone of Hypertrophy; 2) Zone of Ossification; 3) Zone of Calcification.
Order the following 3 hydrogen atoms in order of increasing H-1 NMR shift: 1) Hydrogen atom in formaldehyde; 2) Hydrogen atom in ethylene; 3) Hydrogen atom in benzene.
Order the following 3 numbers by increasing value: 1) 3 to the 7th power; 2) 4 to the 6th power; 3) 5 to the 5th power.
Calculate the combined amplitude of two waves, both with amplitude A, out of phase by π/2.

Identify all of the following three quantities, that, when increased, would increase the slope of the slope of the liquid-gas phase boundary on a phase diagram: 1) Latent heat of vaporization; 2) Change in volume; 3) Change in entropy.

Raphael is observing stars in an eclipsing binary and compiles a brightness timeseries to create a light curve for the pair of stars. Given that Raphael also knows the distance to the system via parallax, but does not have access to spectroscopic data, identify all of the following three properties of the binary that he can accurately determine: 1) Orbital separation; 2) Orbital eccentricity; 3) Stellar masses.
Gause’s Law states which of the following?
set.c.W: Two populations that inhabit the same niche cannot coexist indefinitely
set.c.X: Species adapt to limit niche overlap with other species
set.c.Z: R-selected species are better adapted to exploiting the available resources in an environment
set.a.t: Two populations that inhabit the same niche cannot coexist indefinitely

set.q: Identify all of the following properties that are satisfied by matrix multiplication: 1) Commutativity; 2) Associativity; 3) Additivity.
Order the following three objects by increasing time taken to travel down a ramp: 1) Uniform solid cylinder of length 3 m; 2) Uniform sphere of radius 4 m; 3) Uniform shell of radius 2 m.

Yaw error is the angle difference between the direction a wind turbine's rotor faces and the actual direction of the wind. In wind energy generation, the loss due to yaw error is generally expressed as a power law directly proportional to which of the following trigonometric functions of the error?
Order the following four biomass fuels by increasing entropy in their standard states: 1) Methanol; 2) Biomethane; 3) Syngas; 4) Torrefied pellets.
Identify all of the following three factors that favor plastic deformation over brittle deformation in crustal rocks: 1) Higher temperature; 2) Higher strain rate; 3) Higher fluid content.

Sophia is gazing out at the cosmos and notices that the universe is expanding. Bored, she decides to decrease the critical density of the universe. Identify all of the following changes would help her achieve this goal: 1) Increasing the gravitational constant; 2) Decreasing hubble’s constant; 3) Increasing the speed of light.

Edward mistakes acetone for an amide after seeing a weak IR peak near 3400 cm^-1 alongside the carbonyl stretch at 1700 cm^-1. What is the name for this weak peak, appearing at an integer multiple of a fundamental stretching frequency?

set.a.t: It often causes over-oxidation and oxidative cleavage of the resulting diol into carboxylic acids or ketones

set.q: Order the following three events from earliest to latest to occur in the early universe: 1) Cosmic inflation; 2) Big Bang nucleosynthesis; 3) Quark-hadron transition.

Neurilemma are the outermost layer of a myelin sheath formation, and are technically present in incompletely myelinated nerve axons. In which of the following patterns of myelination can neurilemma be observed, and what type of glial cell exhibits this characteristic?
In a standard Pourbaix diagram, the standard reduction potential of a phase transition is plotted against which of the following quantities?
Rank the following four substituents in order of increasing Cahn–Ingold–Prelog priority: 1) Vinyl; 2) Allyl; 3) Cyano; 4) Benzyl.

The C-rate of a battery refers to the measure of the rate at which it is charged or discharged relative to its maximum capacity. Which of the following best describes the power output and overall efficiency associated with a higher C-rate?
Identify all of the following three heavy elements that are commonly used in commercial thin-film solar cells: 1) Cadmium; 2) Gallium; 3) Tellurium.
Min is playing tennis with a galaxy. The galaxy is observed with a redshift of √13-1. What is the exact speed of the galaxy relative to the observer, in terms of the speed of light c?

By name or number, select all of the following four choices that are principal components of the Yang cycle, or are required in its initiation: 1) ATP; 2) Hydroxyethylene; 3) S-Adenosyl Methionine; 4) Methylthioadenosine.
Order the following 4 ligands by increasing d-orbital splitting: 1) NH3; 2) H2O; 3) Ethylenediamine; 4) F-.

Which of the following are true about Fibonacci numbers? 1) Consecutive Fibonacci numbers are relatively prime; 2) The only Fibonacci numbers that are perfect squares are 0 and 1; 3) The sum of the first n Fibonacci numbers is itself 1 less than a Fibonacci number.

Identify all of the following three assumptions in which the pilot wave theory and Copenhagen interpretation of quantum mechanics differs: 1) Hidden variables; 2) Wave function collapse; 3) Randomness of position.
Rank the following three features in increasing distance from the compact object at the center of an expanding supernova: 1) Forward shock; 2) Reverse shock; 3) Supernova ejecta.

By name or number, select all of the following enzymes that require ATP to function during gluconeogenesis: 1) Pyruvate carboxylase; 2) Phosphoglycerate kinase; 3) Phosphoenolpyruvate carboxy-kinase; 4) Fructose 1,6-Bisphosphate phosphatase.
Identify all of the following three ions that would be considered hard bases: 1) F^-; 2) O^(2-); 3) N^(3-).

Sam is studying the structure and reactivity of cyclic molecules. Identify all of the following three statements that are true about cyclopentadiene: 1) It spontaneously dimerizes at room temperature; 2) It is permanently locked into the s-cis conformation; 3) It is anti-aromatic.

Given that the wavefunction of a particle is time-independent, which of the following 4 statements is always true as the time changes? 1) The expectation value of the position is zero; 2) The expectation value of the momentum is zero; 3) The expectation value of the position is constant; 4) The expectation value of the momentum is a non-zero constant.
Which of the following conditions would be most conducive to the formation of a Fata Morgana?
Identify all of the following three constants that are dimensionless: 1) Fine structure constant; 2) Von-klitzing constant; 3) Planck's constant.

Natural gas power plants are typically based on a combination of the Brayton cycle and Rankine cycles in their operation. Identify all of the following four processes of the Brayton cycle that would correspond lead to an upward motion on a Temperature-Entropy diagram: 1) Isentropic expansion; 2) Isentropic compression; 3) Isobaric heat addition; 4) Isobaric heat rejection.

In windpower generation, solidity refers to the ratio of total blade surface area to the rotor swept area. Which of the following best describes how increasing rotor solidity affects the tip-speed ratio and starting torque for a wind turbine?
By the name or number, select all of the following that are symptoms of dermatomyositis: 1) Chvostek Sign; 2) Raynaud’s Phenomenon; 3) Gottron’s Papules; 4) Heliotrope Rash.
Which of the following sets of species are formed when the permanganate ion acts as an oxidizing agent in acidic and basic solutions, respectively?
Order the following three perchlorate compounds by increasing solubility in aqueous solution: 1) LiClO4; 2) NaClO4; 3) KClO4.

A geothermal well produces a single fluid stream at 180°C. A local municipality wants to implement a cascade system to utilize this resource for multiple community needs before reinjecting the water back into the ground. Order the following four processes from first to last usage to optimize the thermal efficiency of this stream: 1) Electricity generation; 2) Residential heating; 3) Agricultural dehydration; 4) Greenhouse heating.

Travis is frolicking in some streamwater when some waves come to knock him over. Rank the following bedforms by increasing Froude number of the stream flows they are typically found in: 1) Dunes; 2) Ripples; 3) Antidunes; 4) Plane bed.

Henry loves rocks, especially when they show up in Chemistry. Rank the following 3 crystal structures in order of increasing number of oxygen atoms per one formula unit: 1) Perovskite; 2) Spinel; 3) Rutile.
Rank the following three types of water turbines used in hydroelectric power plants by increasing average hydraulic head: 1) Francis; 2) Kaplan; 3) Pelton.
Identify all of the following three changes to a tropical cyclone that are associated with an extratropical transition: 1) Wind field expansion; 2) Reduced pressure aloft; 3) Loss of symmetry.

Ethan is trying to sell fake rocks on the black market by randomly combining minerals. Identify all of the following three mineral pairs that should Ethan avoid putting together, since they are geologically incompatible: 1) Quartz and nepheline; 2) Quartz and corundum; 3) Quartz and olivine.

Because carrier proteins are so ubiquitous for molecular transport, they are often hijacked by viruses. By name or number, select all of the following 4 viruses that hijack/use COP-I for retrograde transport: 1) Influenza; 2) HPV; 3) Rotavirus; 4) Picornavirus.
Order the following three diatomic molecules by increasing theoretical bond order: 1) B2; 2) NO; 3) OF.

Ethan compares the C–Cl bond in 3-chloroprop-1-ene (allyl chloride) with the C–Cl bond in 1-chloropropane, and finds that the allylic C–Cl bond is longer. Which of the following best explains this observation?
set.c.W: Electrons in the C=C π orbital are donated into the C–Cl σ* orbital in coplanar orientation, which weakens and lengthens the C–Cl bond
set.c.X: A chlorine lone pair is donated into the C=C π* orbital, giving the C–Cl bond partial double-bond character
set.c.Y: The adjacent sp^2 carbon withdraws electron density from the CH2 carbon, increasing the s character of its bond to chlorine
set.c.Z: Steric repulsion between the chlorine atom and the vinyl group pushes the chlorine away from the CH2 carbon
set.a.t: Electrons in the C=C π orbital are donated into the C–Cl σ* orbital in coplanar orientation, which weakens and lengthens the C–Cl bond

set.q: Order the following four types of rings from most general to most specific: 1) Principal Ideal Domain; 2) Euclidean Domain; 3) Unique Factorization Domain; 4) Integral Domain.
Which of the following conditions is necessary to observe an Arago spot in the central shadow of an opaque, circular disk?
set.c.W: The Fresnel number must be smaller than 1
set.c.X: The incident light source must constructively interfere across the perimeter
set.c.Y: The radius must be half-integer multiples of the wavelength
set.c.Z: The observation plane must be parallel to the source
set.a.t: The incident light source must constructively interfere across the perimeter

set.c.W: Ischemia more reliably induces latent tetany in hyper-excitable muscles
set.c.X: Continued compression of the radial nerve produces spasms that are clearer to observe
set.c.Y: The radial nerve is more sensitive to calcium concentrations than the facial nerve
set.a.t: Ischemia more reliably induces latent tetany in hyper-excitable muscles

set.q: Ryan has been studying cuprate superconductors and its deviations from BCS theory. Identify all of the following three features that are different between type-I and type-II superconductors: 1) Continuous phase transition into the Meissner state; 2) Flux pinning; 3) Critical magnetic field.

The fill factor is a key parameter in solar cell analysis that measures the "squareness" of the current-voltage curve. Identify all of the following three factors that, when increased, would lead to an increase in the fill factor of a solar cell: 1) Series resistance; 2) Shunt resistance; 3) Temperature.

Identify all of the following three statements that are true of the Eyring equation: 1) It assumes that reactants and the activated transition state complex are in a state of rapid equilibrium; 2) It features both the Boltzmann constant and Planck constant; 3) A negative activation entropy indicates an associative mechanism.
The fractional quantum Hall effect arises from strong Coulomb interactions among two-dimensional electrons under which conditions?

Yamanaka factors is the minimal effective combination of genes that can induce pluripotency, select, by name or number, all of the following that are oncogenetic Yamanaka factors: 1) Oct4; 2) Sox2; 3) Klf4.

set.c.Y: HA: Surface glycoprotein recognition/endocytosis facilitation, NA: Releases newly formed virions
set.a.t: HA: Surface glycoprotein recognition/endocytosis facilitation, NA: Releases newly formed virions

set.q: Which of the following three statements is a correct explanation for the resolution of the twin paradox? 1) The reference frame of the twin on the rocket is non-inertial; 2) The twin in space is moving relative to the earth, so time dilates; 3) The twin is accelerating and thus the time symmetry between the twins are broken.
Jason is taking statistics class. She realizes that since intrinsically brighter objects are easier to detect, there is a selection bias towards them. What is the name of this bias?
Identify all of the following amine classes which may participate as a coupling partner to an aryl halide in a standard Buchwald-Hartwig cross coupling: 1) Primary; 2) Secondary; 3) Tertiary.

Identify all of the following treatments to a solution of isopropyl alcohol that produce a isopropyl halide in an SN2 mechanism: 1) Addition of aqueous HCl; 2) Addition of DEAD in triphenylphosphine with lithium chloride; 3) Addition of anhydrous SOCl2.
Identify all of the following 4 surfaces that are non-orientable? 1) Sphere; 2) Torus; 3) Möbius strip; 4) Klein bottle.
Order the following three regions in a mature supercell thunderstorm by increasing average wind speed: 1) Forward flank downdraft; 2) Rear flank downdraft; 3) Inflow jet.

Akhil performs a Curtius rearrangement on an acyl azide in excess water. Then, after 24 hours, he adds alcohol into the solution, and allows another 24 hours for it to react. Assuming all steps go to completion, which of the following functional groups was NOT present in any of the species present throughout this reaction?
By name or number, select all of the following four that are conditions for a valid equivalence relation: 1) Symmetry; 2) Commutativity; 3) Reflexivity; 4) Transitivity.
Which of the following is true about manifold charts?
set.c.W: Compatibility of charts is an equivalence relation.
set.c.X: Compatibility of charts is not an equivalence relation because it fails the condition of symmetry.
set.c.Y: Compatibility of charts is not an equivalence relation because it fails the condition of reflexivity.
set.c.Z: Compatibility of charts is not an equivalence relation because it fails the condition of transitivity.
set.a.t: Compatibility of charts is not an equivalence relation because it fails the condition of transitivity.

set.q: In tidal power engineering, the analysis of harmonic constituents allow developers to predict wave heights and total energy yields prior to tidal plant construction. Rank the following three harmonic constituents by increasing period: 1) M2; 2) N2; 3) S2.
Order the following three regions of a charged, rotating black hole in increasing distance from the singularity: 1) Event horizon; 2) Cauchy horizon; 3) Photon sphere.
Sam is studying liquid crystals for their use in smart glass window panels. Identify all of the following liquid crystal phases that exhibit positional order: 1) Smectic; 2) Discotic; 3) Nematic.

Oh no! Haru is pouring a strong base on Min’s much needed alcohol. Which of the following could protect alcohols from strong bases? 1) Reacting the alcohol under DHP under acid catalysis; 2) Reacting the alcohol with an acyl chloride and pyridine; 3) Reacting the alcohol with a silyl chloride under a weak base; 4) Williamson ether synthesis with a benzyl halide.
Which of the following three particles may be a weyl fermion? 1) Electron; 2) Charm quark; 3) Tau neutrino.

Hydrogen gas is classified into various colors based on its production origin, feedstock, and energy inputs. Identify all of the following four hydrogen gas colors that are primarily derived from natural gas feedstock: 1) Blue; 2) Green; 3) Pink; 4) White.

A single-basin tidal power plant has a basin surface area of 3.0 × 10^7 m^2. The local tidal range is 9 m, and the power plant's turbines stop operating when the hydraulic head falls below 3 m. If the basin area is decreased to 5.0 × 10^6 m^2 due to sediment deposition around the basin, and the local tidal range subsequently increases to 15 m, then what is the ratio of the new maximum operation potential energy of the tidal basin to the old potential energy for tidal generation?

Kian has a sample of carbon dioxide at constant pressure, and is trying to calculate its volume. In order to simplify his work, he assumes all intermolecular forces are negligible, but that the CO2 molecules take up a significant volume. Assuming he has all relevant constants related to the gas, rank the following 3 relations he can use in order of increasing calculated volume of carbon dioxide that he would obtain: 1) Ideal Gas Law; 2) Van Der Waals Equation; 3) Infinite Virial Power Series.

Travis uses a really really good hair dryer to open up the ring of cis-3,4-dimethylcyclobutene via a thermal electrocyclic mechanism. Select all of the following alkenes that could be produced: 1) (2E,4E)-hexa-2,4-diene; 2) (2E,4Z)-hexa-2,4,diene; 3) (2Z,4Z)-hexa-2,4,diene.
Groups of which of the following three numbers of elements are guaranteed to be abelian? 1) 5; 2) 25; 3) 45.

In a current-biased DC SQUID, applying a magnetic flux Φ causes the critical current to oscillate with a periodicity equal to the magnetic flux quantum Φ_0. In terms of Planck's constant h and elementary charge e, what is the exact form of Φ_0?
Min Shin loves nice euhedral crystals. Order the following four minerals in increasing tendency to form euhedral crystals. 1) Cordierite; 2) Quartz; 3) Tourmaline; 4) Rutile.

Chris is shooting a reenactment of Arman biking off a bridge, performing a water bucket clutch after falling. Assuming g = 10 m/s^2, if he was biking at 20 m/s and the drop was 125 meters in real life, and he wants the scene to last 1 second while appearing realistic, answer the following two questions. 1) What should the height of the bridge be?; 2) How fast should Arman be biking on the set?.

Identify all of the following three statements that are true about solar cells in the diffusion-limited regime: 1) The temperature coefficient correlates inversely with cell voltage; 2) Collection probability degrades exponentially with cell thickness; 3) Bifacial gain scales directly with ground coverage ratio.

Min Shin has access to many supercomputing nodes, so he approximates the H_2^+ ground-state wavefunction as a linear combination of 100,000 basis functions and solves the secular equations at a fixed internuclear distance. Compared with the exact ground-state energy for that geometry, which best describes the lowest energy he obtains?
set.a.t: At or slightly above it, approaching it as the basis grows

set.q: Min Shinian adds :CH2 (from photolysis of diazomethane) to cis-2-butene in two runs: once immediately in the liquid phase, and once after diluting with excess inert gas so the carbene relaxes to its ground state. Which best explains the stereochemical outcomes?

When modeling hydrodynamics, engineers often apply specific model laws based on the dominant force governing a given flow regime. Identify all of the following dimensionless numbers used in fluid dynamics that are directly proportional to the density of the fluid: 1) Reynolds number; 2) Froude number; 3) Euler number; 4) Weber number.

Ziang is studying resonant Trans-Neptunian objects in the Kuiper belt and scattered disc. Rank the following four mean-motion resonances with Neptune in increasing order of the number of observed trans-Neptunian objects currently occupying them: 1) 1 to 10; 2) 2 to 7; 3) 3 to 4; 4) 5 to 9.

Identify all of the following five statements that correctly describe the physical chemistry, radiative balance, or internal structural properties of Titan: 1) Solar ultraviolet photolysis of stratospheric methane can initiate polymerization of hydrocarbons into tholins; 2) Titan's tidal locking results in superrotation in the upper atmosphere, blocking methane convection; 3) Mountains and valleys on Titan's surface are carved out of massive methane ice sheets due to near-triple-point surface conditions; 4) Titan experiences a powerful atmospheric greenhouse effect driven by the collision-induced absorption of infrared radiation.
Select all of the following three types of introns that form a lariat: 1) Type I; 2) U1; 3) U2.
Order the following three atmospheric boundaries in increasing average temperature: 1) Tropopause; 2) Stratopause; 3) Mesopause.

Shown in the image is a cloud. Answer the following three questions about this cloud. I) What is the name of this cloud? II) At which of the following ranges of latitudes are these clouds completely visible: 1) 30–50°; 2) 50–70°; 3) 70–90°? III) On which of the following wavelengths are these clouds most reflective: W) Ultraviolet; X) Infrared; Y) Radio; Z) Microwave?

The image shown is an MRI of an individual with a very rare affliction caused by a defective ECM1 gene which causes the accumulation of hyaline collagenous material. Answer the following three questions about this image. I) What disease is this? II) What specific brain component is damaged? III) What specific type of MRI was used to construct this image?
set.a.t: I) URBACH-WIETHE DISEASE; II) AMYGDALA; III) SWI (SUSCEPTIBILITY WEIGHTED IMAGING)

set.q: The experiment depicted in the image determines the adiabatic index of a gas by measuring the oscillations of a ball in a glass tube with one side exposed to air and the other to a chamber with the gas. What is this experiment?

Shown in the image is a Sankey diagram depicting energy flow and consumption through various systems and sectors in the state of Hawaii. Answer the following two questions about this diagram: I) To the nearest percent, what is the net thermal conversion efficiency of Hawaii's electrical generation sector? II) Ground transportation consumes approximately 55 trillion BTUs of liquid fossil fuels. Assuming internal combustion engine vehicles operate at an average tank-to-wheel thermal efficiency of 20%, and electric vehicles (EVs) operate at a grid-to-wheel efficiency of 80%, which of the following best describes the electrical energy an EV would consume to deliver the same mechanical work, and the net primary energy savings: W) 11 trillion BTUs required; net savings of 44 trillion BTUs; X) 14 trillion BTUs required; net savings of 41 trillion BTUs; Y) 27 trillion BTUs required; net savings of 28 trillion BTUs; Z) 44 trillion BTUs required; net savings of 11 trillion BTUs?

Shown in the image is a rock near the ocean. Answer the following two questions about this structure. I) What is the name for the cavities formed in the rock? II) In intertidal zones, the mechanical formation of these cavities is frequently accelerated by the bio-erosive grazing action of which class of mollusks?
What theorem in graph theory states that a graph is planar if and only if it contains no subgraph that is a subdivision of either of the two graphs shown, K_5 or K_(3,3)?

Shown are two different types of computed tomography scans used for analysis of blood flow. The right would be used for initially ruling out hemorrhages, and the left for more closely analyzing embolisms and thrombosis. What specific subtypes of CT scans are the left and right images, respectively?

Shown in the images is the decay of the phi meson. Answer the following two questions about the images. 1) On the right image are two of the same mesons with different charges. What is the identity of this meson? 2) While both decay paths are possible, the second decay is much more probable. This is because of what rule, stating that any strongly occurring process will be suppressed if, through only the removal of internal gluon lines, its Feynman diagram can be separated into two disconnected diagrams with one containing all initial-state particles and another containing all final-state particles?

Shown in the image is a diagram of a Vanadium Redox Flow Battery, or VRFB, which is a device commonly used to buffer intermittent power generation from wind and PV plants. Answer the following three questions about this image: I) Based on the solid arrows showing proton migration from the catholyte to the anolyte chamber across the ion exchange membrane, do the solid line paths represent the battery charging or discharging? II) What vanadium ion species undergoes oxidation in the anolyte solution during battery discharge? III) If the volume of electrolyte in both tanks is doubled while keeping the size of the central RF-cell constant, which of the following best describes how the system's power capacity and energy capacity, respectively, are affected: W) Doubles, doubles; X) Doubles, quadruples; Y) Doubles, stays the same; Z) Stays the same, doubles?
set.a.t: I) CHARGING; II) V^(2+); III) Z

set.q: Shown in the image is a hydrodynamical simulation of a single "finger" of a certain fluid instability. Identify all of the following four processes that occur because of this instability: 1) Volcanic eruptions; 2) Diapirism; 3) Billow clouds; 4) Salt fingering.

In the image shown is a unique conjugated system of 2p orbitals arranged in a Möbius strip experiencing Möbius conjugation and aromaticity. Answer the following three questions about this system. I) According to the Woodward-Hoffmann rules, did the formation of this ring likely occur via a suprafacial or antarafacial pathway? II) Identify all of the following pi-electron counts in a ring system for which thermal Möbius aromaticity would apply: 1) 6; 2) 8; 3) 10. III) How many bonding, nonbonding, and antibonding orbitals, respectively, exist in a 6-membered Möbius-aromatic system?

Shown in the image is a Turbine Performance Hill Chart, which maps hydraulic efficiency, guide vane opening angle, and discharge against rotational turbine speed in hydroelectric power plants. Answer the following two questions about this diagram: I) Assuming the density of water is 1000 kg/m^3, to two significant figures, calculate the hydraulic power input in kilowatts supplied to the turbine at an operating discharge of 2.5 m^3/s under an effective net head of 20 m. II) Given that the turbine operates at a synchronous grid frequency yielding a constant speed of 260 rpm, to one significant figure, what is the minimum guide vane angle in degrees required to achieve a hydraulic efficiency of at least 70%?

Shown in the image are the HR diagrams for a sample of stars from two different types of clusters. Answer the following three questions regarding these HR diagrams: I) What types of star clusters are represented by the green and red sections of the color-magnitude diagram, respectively? II) Given that the star of the highest V-band absolute magnitude in the cluster represented in red has an apparent V-band magnitude of 9.5, in parsecs and to one significant figure, calculate the distance to this cluster. III) What mathematical model is used to characterize the standard surface brightness profile for a cluster of the type represented in green?
set.a.t: I) GREEN IS GLOBULAR, RED IS OPEN; II) 300 PARSECS; III) KING PROFILE

set.q: Shown in the image are two magnetic spin structures. Identify the magnetic state of each structure from top to bottom, respectively.

Answer the following two questions about the dunes in the image. I) What specific geomorphological term classifies this type of dune? II) According to Bagnold's formula, the mass transport rate of sand by wind saltation is proportional to what power of the wind's friction velocity?

The image shown is the orientation diagram for Förster Resonance Energy Transfer. I) Give the maximum and minimum values for the orientation factor in this general conformation. II) What is the ensemble average of the orientation factor in this general conformation? III) What is the orientation factor if theta_D is 90 degrees, theta_A is 60 degrees, and theta_T is 30 degrees?

Min Shinian collects random molecules in his organic chemistry class and studies their stereochemical behavior. Answer the following three questions about the three molecules shown in the image. 1) What is the name of the general class of compounds to which compound 1 belongs? 2) Identify all of the compounds 1, 2 and 3 in the image that are chiral. 3) Compound 2 can be bound to ruthenium to form the catalyst used in Noyori hydrogenation. Min Shinian combines the (R)-configuration of compound 2 with a Ru(II) precursor to make the compound shown in the image. He then uses this catalyst to hydrogenate methyl acetoacetate (shown in the image) under H_2. Which of the following is the major product: W) (R)-methyl 3-hydroxybutanoate; X) (S)-methyl 3-hydroxybutanoate; Y) (R)-1,3-butanediol; Z) racemic methyl 3-hydroxybutanoate?

Shown in the image is a metal rod inserted into a 2% polyacrylamide solution. This image depicts the Weissenberg effect, where a fluid is drawn towards an inserted, spinning rod. The Weissenberg effect occurs for what type of non-Newtonian fluid, which is elastic when a load is applied for a short period of time and viscous when it is applied for long periods of time?

Shown in the image are various maps of the surface properties of Mimas, a moon of Saturn and the smallest astronomical body known to be roughly rounded in shape due to its own gravity. Answer the following two questions about Mimas: I) Which of the following options best explains the lopsided distribution of surface temperatures on Mimas: W) High-energy electrons selectively bombard the leading hemisphere, increasing the thermal inertia of surface ice; X) Distinct patches of low-albedo dust deposited by Saturn's E-ring absorb sunlight unevenly across the moon's surface; Y) Tidal flexing from Saturn drives localized friction and uneven venting of warm water vapor through deep fractures; Z) Sublimation causes the preferential migration and settling of volatile frost on anti-subsolar longitudes? II) When an impactor struck Mimas to form the Herschel crater, it generated massive shock waves. Given that the mass of Mimas is approximately 4.0 × 10^19 kg and its mean radius is approximately 2 × 10^5 m, to two significant figures and in scientific notation, what would have been the minimum gravitational binding energy in joules required to completely overcome Mimas' self-gravity and catastrophically fracture the moon from the impact site through to its antipode?

Shown in the image is a Feynman diagram of deep inelastic scattering. At high energies, the scattering of electrons off partons inside the nucleon rather than the whole nucleon is independent of the momentum transfer. What is this phenomenon called?

Shown in the image is a pressure-enthalpy diagram depicting the thermodynamic phase boundaries and isotherms for a refrigerant used in a geothermal binary system. Answer the following three questions about this diagram: I) What term is used to refer to the isenthalpic process represented by the red arrow? II) In this binary power plant, the refrigerant undergoes an isenthalpic expansion through a throttling valve, with an initial enthalpy of 50 BTU/lb, moving to a lower-pressure separator where the saturated liquid and saturated vapor enthalpies are 20 BTU/lb and 100 BTU/lb, respectively. After this process, what is the resulting vapor quality of the liquid-vapor refrigerant mixture? III) Geothermal power plants require a working fluid to absorb heat from the ground and vaporize, driving turbines and generating electricity. What type of mixture is commonly used as the working fluid in geothermal systems because its boiling profile closely matches the declining temperature profile of the geothermal resource, minimizing exergy destruction?
set.a.t: I) FLASHING; II) 3/8; III) ZEOTROPIC MIXTURE

set.q: Given is a 6-layer diagram of the lateral geniculate nucleus. Answer the following two questions about this image. I) What do A, B, and C stand for, respectively? II) What type of retinal ganglion cells are involved in visual processing via the B and C pathways, respectively?
set.a.t: I) KONIOCELLULAR, PARVOCELLULAR, MAGNOCELLULAR; II) MIDGET CELLS, PARASOL CELLS

set.q: The image shows a sheet of graphene rolled along a specific chiral vector to form a cylinder. Researchers covalently attach aryl groups from aryl diazonium salts, creating sp^3 defects in the wall, and observe new emission features. Answer the following three questions: 1) What is the general name of the structure shown in the image? 2) The sp^3 defect produces a new emission at lower energy than the native transition. Which of the following best explains this: W) The aryl group itself fluoresces, and its emission overlaps with the nanotube's; X) The sp^3 defect creates a local potential well that traps the mobile exciton, lowering its energy before it recombines and emits; Y) Functionalization converts the semiconducting nanotube into a metallic one, narrowing its band gap; Z) The electron-withdrawing aryl substituent raises the energy of the nanotube's conduction band, increasing the emission energy? 3) Researchers compare sp^3 defects on the same nanotube made with 4-nitrophenyl and 4-methoxyphenyl groups. Which produces the larger redshift in emission?

Travis likes to draw equilateral triangles. He takes a triangle ABC and constructs equilateral triangles outwardly on each side of the triangle, so that BCX, CAY, and ABZ are equilateral, as shown in the image. First, what theorem states that the centers of the three equilateral triangles themselves form an equilateral triangle? Next, at what point do the lines AX, BY, and CZ intersect?

Shown in the image is a graph depicting the molar Mg/Ca ratio in seawater over the past 500 million years. Answer the following two questions about this graph: I) Which of the following events most heavily influenced the sharp decrease in Mg/Ca ratios between 200 and 100 million years ago: W) Suppressed dolomitization in shallow marine environments; X) Shifts in mid-ocean ridge activity after the breakup of Pangaea; Y) Enhanced chemical weathering and CO_2 sequestration from tectonic exposure; Z) Widespread oceanic anoxic events due to increased continental runoff? II) Identify all of the following factors that generally increase Mg/Ca ratios in benthic foraminifera: 1) Increased foraminiferal metabolic rates; 2) Higher carbonate ion saturation in seawater; 3) Greater partial dissolution of the foraminiferal test.

Shown in the image is a Van Krevelen diagram, which compares the atomic ratios of hydrogen-to-carbon and oxygen-to-carbon in various organic materials used in fossil fuels as well as biomass energy conversion. Answer the following three questions about this image: I) What process corresponds to the down-left movement of species on the diagram, upgrading raw biomass into high-grade, solid fuel under anoxic conditions? II) Sedimentary kerogen is a form of fossilized organic matter that is commonly used to generate petroleum and natural gas. Order the following three types of kerogen by increasing hydrogen-to-carbon ratio: 1) Type I; 2) Type II; 3) Type III. III) Each of the arrows, labeled A, B, and C, represents a process associated with the loss of different functional groups from organic molecules undergoing thermal processing. Match the following three processes with their respective letters A, B, and C: 1) Dehydration; 2) Decarboxylation; 3) Demethylation.
set.a.t: I) TORREFACTION; II) 3, 2, 1; III) A = 2, B = 3, C = 1

set.q: The image shows a single-atom-thick sheet made entirely of boron, grown on a silver surface. Answer the following three questions: 1) What is the general name of the two-dimensional material shown in the image? 2) Because boron is electron deficient, what type of bond is found in this material, similar to the one in diborane? 3) Min Shin decides to grow the boron sheet on a substrate that donates more electrons than silver. How should the sheet's structure change: W) Fewer hexagonal holes, because extra electrons support more B–B bonds; X) More hexagonal holes, because donated electrons fill bonding states a honeycomb would leave empty; Y) No change, because lattice mismatch alone sets the hole pattern; Z) Buckling into a diamond-like sheet, because extra electrons favor sp^3 boron?

set.a.t: Current source in parallel with resistor
